notes: Product/technical: building a VS Code extension used by internal devs and 3rd-party customers (marketplace).
Primary UX: streaming completions (token-by-token), inline suggestions with accept/reject metrics, and low-latency mini-sessions for edits.
Latency target: median completion latency <120ms for 8-16 token suggestions in NA; P99 <450ms. Customer stressed network jitter tolerance.
Throughput: concurrent active editors estimated 500 daily active users in phase 1. Peak sustained requests ~50rps for completions during internal dogfood.
Cost sensitivity: wants clear token-level cost estimate; target incremental cost <$0.08 per user/month for typical usage (suggestions + light completion).
Model preferences: prefer open Llama-family variants but want Redwood to host multiple pinned versions and automatable rollouts (canary then full).
Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to quantized model on Dedicated if hosted capacity constrained; fallbacks should preserve streaming interface.
Security/compliance: must support SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, and 12 month audit log retention for enterprise customers.
Integration notes: extension team wants a tiny JS streaming SDK (websocket + chunked HTTP) with reconnect semantics and backpressure signals.
Edge cases: offline editor mode should use local prefix cache for immediate suggestions; customer will accept degraded non-streaming responses if disconnected.
Quoting / procurement: legal requested DPA + standard security FAQ; procurement expects final SOC2 evidence before Dedicated purchase.
Customer quote (paraphrase): 'We need consistent completion behavior across releases — pinning + rollout controls are non-negotiable.'
